$schema: see scripts/test-event-detect.ts for the reader and the scoring rules
about: Gold events for the narrative event engine. Hand-annotated per chapter against
the paragraph numbering that scripts/print-chapter.ts prints, which is the same
split the engine uses (/\n{2,}|\n/ + trim + drop-empties). A shifted anchor
would make every score a plausible-looking near-miss, so that split is shared.
DEFINITION. An event is a change of state a reader would mention when asked what
happens in the chapter. This is close to LitBank's 'asserted realis' event
(Sims, Park & Bamman, ACL 2019) with one deliberate divergence: LitBank excludes
negated events, and this set keeps them, because a refusal ('she did not answer')
is one of the strongest beats in this corpus. Salience follows Barthes' cardinal
function as used by Otake et al. (COLING 2020): major = removing it changes what
afterwards makes sense.
EXCLUDED, and these are the traps: scene-setting however vivid, backstory,
interior musing that changes nothing, a topic merely being discussed, and the
chapter merely starting or ending.
KNOWN LIMITATION. Both source manuscripts are in-distribution for the ENGINE THIS
REPLACES, whose phrase dictionaries were tuned on them (45% of its multi-word
phrases occur in Hollow Iris and not in The Root Crown). The replacement engine
carries no manuscript-derived phrases, so this set measures it fairly, but it
cannot by itself prove generalisation. scripts/ood-event-audit.ts covers that
with label-free metrics over both full books.

EVENTFULNESS VARIES ON PURPOSE. 2, 5, 9, 3, 6, 4, 2, 6, 2, 3, 3 events across 11 chapters. A detector that emits a fixed three per chapter cannot score well here, and the engine this replaces emitted 2.67 on average regardless of content.

typeNotes.decision: someone binds themselves to a course of action
typeNotes.revelation: someone learns, or makes another know, something that changes belief
typeNotes.confrontation: two parties come into open opposition
typeNotes.action: a physical or documentary act with consequences
typeNotes.arrival: someone or something enters the situation
typeNotes.state-change: a condition of the world changes

events.summary: Wilson finds the League's office shut, with a notice that it is dissolved
events.evidence: THE RED-HEADED LEAGUE IS DISSOLVED. October 9, 1890.

events.summary: Holmes reacts with excitement to the description of Wilson's assistant, recognizing him
events.evidence: Holmes sat up in his chair in considerable excitement.

events.summary: Holmes reveals he was scrutinizing the assistant's worn trouser knees
events.evidence: The knees of his trousers.

events.summary: Holmes reveals a major crime is being planned and that he means to stop it
events.evidence: A considerable crime is in contemplation.

events.summary: Holmes brings Jones and Merryweather in to join the night's operation
events.evidence: Let me introduce you to Mr. Merryweather, who is to be our companion in to-night’s adventure.

events.summary: A vault floor stone is lifted and the tunnelling intruders emerge
events.evidence: one of the broad, white stones turned over upon its side and left a square, gaping hole

events.summary: Holmes seizes the intruder, John Clay, in the vault
events.evidence: Sherlock Holmes had sprung out and seized the intruder by the collar.

events.summary: John Clay is handcuffed and taken into custody
events.evidence: as the handcuffs clattered upon his wrists

chapters.whatHappens: Mary Sutherland tells Holmes how her fiance Hosmer Angel vanished on their wedding morning; Holmes deduces and exposes that Angel was actually her own stepfather in disguise, who flees when confronted.

events.summary: Miss Mary Sutherland arrives at Baker Street to consult Holmes
events.evidence: the boy in buttons entered to announce Miss Mary Sutherland

events.summary: Mary Sutherland becomes engaged to Hosmer Angel
events.evidence: We were engaged after the first walk that we took.

events.summary: Hosmer Angel vanishes from the cab on the wedding morning, never seen again
events.evidence: we waited for him to step out, but he never did

events.summary: Holmes commits to investigating the case for Miss Sutherland
events.evidence: I shall glance into the case for you

events.summary: Miss Sutherland reveals she had already advertised for Hosmer Angel
events.evidence: I advertised for him in last Saturday’s _Chronicle_

events.summary: Holmes writes to Windibank arranging a meeting at Baker Street
events.evidence: asking him whether he could meet us here at six o’clock to-morrow evening

events.summary: Mr. James Windibank arrives at Baker Street for the appointment
events.evidence: The man who entered was a sturdy, middle-sized fellow

events.summary: Holmes reveals he has already caught Hosmer Angel, exposing Windibank
events.evidence: I let you know, then, that I have caught him!

events.summary: Windibank threatens Holmes with legal liability for locking the door
events.evidence: it is you who are breaking the law now, and not me

events.summary: Windibank flees Baker Street at a run, escaping Holmes's whip
events.evidence: from the window we could see Mr. James Windibank running at the top of his speed down the road

chapters.whatHappens: An old, secretive sea captain takes lodging at the Admiral Benbow, pays Jim to watch for a one-legged seaman, and one night draws a knife on Dr. Livesey before backing down under threat of the gallows.

events.summary: The old sea captain arrives at the inn and takes lodging
events.evidence: came plodding to the inn door, his sea-chest following behind him

events.summary: Captain declares he'll stay and pays with gold coins on account
events.evidence: I’ll stay here a bit

events.summary: Captain pays Jim to watch for a one-legged seafaring man
events.evidence: keep my “weather-eye open for a seafaring man with one leg”

events.summary: Captain draws a knife and threatens to pin the doctor to the wall
events.evidence: threatened to pin the doctor to the wall

events.summary: Captain backs down, puts away his knife, and returns to his seat
events.evidence: the captain soon knuckled under, put up his weapon

chapters.whatHappens: A stranger called Black Dog corners the ailing captain at the inn; the two fight with cutlasses until Black Dog flees wounded, and the shock brings on a stroke that Dr. Livesey treats, warning the captain that more rum will kill him.

events.summary: A pale stranger (Black Dog) enters the inn asking for the captain
events.evidence: a man stepped in on whom I had never set my eyes

events.summary: Captain turns pale and sick with fear on seeing Black Dog
events.evidence: all the brown had gone out of his face

events.summary: Captain and Black Dog fight with cutlasses; Black Dog is wounded
events.evidence: the captain hotly pursuing, both with drawn cutlasses

events.summary: Black Dog escapes over the hill despite his wound
events.evidence: disappeared over the edge of the hill in half a minute

events.summary: The captain collapses, felled by a stroke, after the fight
events.evidence: beheld the captain lying full length upon the floor

events.summary: Dr. Livesey arrives just as the stricken captain needs help
events.evidence: the door opened and Doctor Livesey came in

events.summary: Doctor warns the captain that more rum will kill him
events.evidence: if you don’t break off short, you’ll die

chapters.whatHappens: The dying captain confides to Jim that he was Flint's first mate and guards a treasure secret; Jim's father dies that night; the next day a blind beggar forces his way in and delivers the black spot, and the shock kills the captain on the spot.

events.summary: Jim agrees to bring the captain just one glass of rum
events.evidence: I’ll get you one glass, and no more

events.summary: Captain reveals he was old Flint's first mate and knows the treasure's secret
events.evidence: I was first mate, I was, old Flint’s first mate

events.summary: Jim's father dies suddenly that evening
events.evidence: my poor father died quite suddenly that evening

events.summary: A blind beggar appears on the road outside the inn
events.evidence: He was plainly blind, for he tapped before him with a stick

events.summary: Blind man threatens to break Jim's arm unless led to the captain
events.evidence: Take me in straight or I’ll break your arm.

events.summary: Blind man secretly presses the black spot into the captain's hand
events.evidence: into the palm of the captain’s, which closed upon it instantly

events.summary: Blind man slips away as swiftly as he came
events.evidence: skipped out of the parlour and into the road

events.summary: The captain dies of a sudden stroke (apoplexy)
events.evidence: The captain had been struck dead by thundering apoplexy

chapters.whatHappens: With the neighbours too frightened to help, Jim and his mother return alone to the inn, find the black spot's deadline and the chest's key, and discover gold and a papers packet in the captain's chest before fleeing just ahead of returning smugglers, hiding under a bridge when Jim's mother faints.

events.summary: Villagers refuse to help defend the inn against the smugglers
events.evidence: no soul would consent to return with us to the Admiral Benbow

events.summary: Jim's mother resolves that she and Jim will go back to the inn alone
events.evidence: We’ll have that chest open, if we die for it.

events.summary: The black spot's message reveals a ten o'clock deadline
events.evidence: You have till ten tonight.

events.summary: They find the captain's chest key hidden on a string around his neck
events.evidence: hanging to a bit of tarry string

events.summary: They discover an oilcloth packet of papers and a bag of gold in the chest
events.evidence: a bundle tied up in oilcloth, and looking like papers

events.summary: The blind man tries the bolted door but fails to get in
events.evidence: the handle being turned and the bolt rattling

events.summary: Jim grabs the oilskin packet as they flee the inn
events.evidence: I’ll take this to square the count

events.summary: Jim's mother faints; he drags her under a bridge to hide from the pursuers
events.evidence: drag her down the bank and a little way under the arch

chapters.whatHappens: Buccaneers led by the blind Pew break into the inn and find the treasure item already gone; a warning signal scatters them, and Pew is trampled to death by arriving revenue officers, who then chase the smugglers' lugger to Kitt's Hole but let it escape after being fired on.

events.summary: Blind man orders the buccaneers to break down the inn door
events.evidence: Down with the door!

events.summary: Buccaneers discover the treasure item ('Flint's fist') is missing from the chest
events.evidence: they’ve been before us. Someone’s turned the chest out alow and aloft.

events.summary: A warning whistle sounds twice, signalling danger to the buccaneers
events.evidence: a signal to warn them of approaching danger

events.summary: Pew, enraged, strikes his own men with his stick
events.evidence: he struck at them right and left in his blindness

events.summary: The buccaneers panic and scatter, abandoning Pew
events.evidence: the buccaneers turned at once and ran, separating in every direction

events.summary: Riders (revenue officers) appear, galloping down the slope
events.evidence: four or five riders came in sight in the moonlight

events.summary: Pew is trampled under the horses and dies
events.evidence: He fell on his side, then gently collapsed upon his face

events.summary: The lugger escapes after firing a shot near Supervisor Dance
events.evidence: a bullet whistled close by his arm

chapters.whatHappens: The Hispaniola sights Treasure Island; Silver, recognizing the place, conceals his disappointment that the captain's chart omits the treasure markings; Jim secretly warns Dr. Livesey, then reveals Silver's mutiny plot to the officers, who realize they are outnumbered and decide to wait rather than risk open conflict.

events.summary: The crew sights land: the hills of Treasure Island
events.evidence: we saw two low hills, about a couple of miles apart

events.summary: Silver hides his disappointment that the chart lacks the treasure markings
events.evidence: Silver had the strength of mind to hide it

events.summary: Jim secretly asks Dr. Livesey to arrange a private meeting, hinting at terrible news
events.evidence: I have terrible news.

events.summary: Captain announces a toast as pretext to gather the officers in the cabin
events.evidence: he and I and the doctor are going below to the cabin

events.summary: Jim reveals the full details of Silver's mutiny plot to the officers
events.evidence: told the whole details of Silver’s conversation

events.summary: The squire admits he was wrong and defers to the captain
events.evidence: you were right, and I was wrong

events.summary: Captain decides they must wait and avoid open conflict for now
events.evidence: Lay to, and whistle for a wind, that’s my view.

events.summary: They realize only seven of twenty-six aboard can be trusted
events.evidence: the grown men on our side were six to their nineteen

chapters.whatHappens: Jim secretly watches Silver try to win over the honest hand Tom, who refuses and, after hearing a scream that signals a shipmate's murder, openly renounces Silver; Silver clubs Tom down with his crutch and finishes him with a knife, then whistles for reinforcements as Jim flees in terror.

events.summary: Tom refuses to join Silver's mutiny despite the danger
events.evidence: I’d sooner lose my hand

events.summary: A horrible scream from the marsh signals that Alan has been killed
events.evidence: then one horrid, long-drawn scream

events.summary: Tom openly renounces Silver and turns to walk away
events.evidence: you’re mate of mine no more

events.summary: Silver hurls his crutch, striking Tom down with a stunning blow
events.evidence: struck poor Tom, point foremost, and with stunning violence

events.summary: Silver finishes Tom off, stabbing him twice with his knife
events.evidence: twice buried his knife up to the hilt

events.summary: Silver blows a whistle to summon more of the crew
events.evidence: brought out a whistle, and blew upon it several modulated blasts

events.summary: Jim flees the hiding place, running as fast as he can
events.evidence: I ran as I never ran before

chapters.whatHappens: The narrator recounts, in hindsight, how astronomers first detected unexplained flashes of gas on Mars, and how he personally witnessed one such flash through Ogilvy's telescope -- the first sign of the Martians launching their invasion of Earth.

events.summary: Astronomers observe an unexplained great light on Mars during the 1894 opposition
events.evidence: a great light was seen on the illuminated part of the disk

events.summary: Lavelle observes a huge outbreak of incandescent gas launched from Mars toward Earth
events.evidence: a huge outbreak of incandescent gas upon the planet

events.summary: Ogilvy invites the narrator to join him in observing Mars through his telescope that night
events.evidence: invited me up to take a turn with him that night in a scrutiny of the red planet

events.summary: The narrator personally witnesses another jet of gas fired from Mars toward Earth
events.evidence: there was another jetting out of gas from the distant planet. I saw it.

chapters.whatHappens: Ogilvy discovers that the falling star seen overnight was in fact a huge artificial cylinder buried in Horsell Common; watching it, he realizes its top is being unscrewed from within and connects it to the strange flashes seen on Mars, then runs for help, and by the time Henderson telegraphs the news to London, crowds are already heading out to see the dead men from Mars.

events.summary: A blazing falling star is seen streaking across the sky and falling to earth near Woking
events.evidence: rushing over Winchester eastward, a line of flame high in the atmosphere

events.summary: Ogilvy finds the fallen object: an enormous hole gouged out by the impact of a huge cylinder
events.evidence: An enormous hole had been made by the impact of the projectile

events.summary: Ogilvy realizes the cylinder is artificial and hollow, its top being unscrewed from within
events.evidence: The cylinder was artificial—hollow—with an end that screwed out!

events.summary: Ogilvy connects the cylinder to the flash of gas he had seen on Mars
events.evidence: he linked the Thing with the flash upon Mars

events.summary: Ogilvy runs for help, dismissed as mad until he reaches the journalist Henderson
events.evidence: set off running wildly into Woking

events.summary: Returning to the cylinder, Ogilvy and Henderson find a ring of bright metal now showing at its rim
events.evidence: a thin circle of bright metal showed between the top and the body of the cylinder

events.summary: Henderson telegraphs the news of the cylinder to London
events.evidence: Henderson went into the railway station at once, in order to telegraph the news to London.

events.summary: Crowds of boys and unemployed men set out for the common to see the dead men from Mars
events.evidence: a number of boys and unemployed men had already started for the common

events.summary: The narrator hears the news and heads out to the sand-pits himself
events.evidence: lost no time in going out and across the Ottershaw bridge to the sand-pits

chapters.whatHappens: A human deputation approaches the Martian pit under a flag of truce and is annihilated by the Heat-Ray, which sets the common ablaze while the narrator escapes.

events.summary: deputation advances on pit waving white flag
events.evidence: advancing from the direction of Horsell, I noted a little black knot of men, the foremost of whom was waving a white flag.

events.summary: Heat-Ray apparatus rises and flickers from pit
events.evidence: Slowly a humped shape rose out of the pit, and the ghost of a beam of light seemed to flicker out from it.

events.summary: Heat-Ray incinerates the deputation of men
events.evidence: flashes of actual flame, a bright glare leaping from one to another, sprang from the scattered group of men.

events.summary: fires ignite across the common and buildings
events.evidence: every dry furze bush became with one dull thud a mass of flames.

events.summary: Heat-Ray shuts off, device sinks into pit
events.evidence: the hissing and humming ceased, and the black, dome-like object sank slowly out of sight into the pit.

events.summary: narrator turns and flees across the heath
events.evidence: With an effort I turned and began a stumbling run through the heather.

chapters.whatHappens: Riding back to Maybury the narrator sees a third cylinder fall and a fighting-machine up close, crashes his cart, finds the innkeeper dead, and bolts himself into his house.

events.summary: Narrator departs Leatherhead alone for Maybury
events.evidence: It was nearly eleven when I started to return.

events.summary: Third Martian cylinder falls nearby
events.evidence: It was the third falling star!

events.summary: Horse bolts, terrified by thunder
events.evidence: The horse took the bit between his teeth and bolted.

events.summary: Narrator sees first Martian fighting-machine clearly
events.evidence: A monstrous tripod, higher than many houses, striding over the young pine trees, and smashing them aside in its career

events.summary: Dog cart crashes, horse killed
events.evidence: the dog cart had heeled over upon the horse; the shafts smashed noisily

events.summary: Narrator evades machines, reaches woods unseen
events.evidence: succeeded in crawling, unobserved by these monstrous machines, into the pine woods towards Maybury

events.summary: Dead man identified as innkeeper landlord
events.evidence: It was the landlord of the Spotted Dog, whose conveyance I had taken.

events.summary: Narrator reaches home, bolts himself in
events.evidence: I let myself in with my latchkey, closed, locked and bolted the door, staggered to the foot of the staircase, and sat down.
